No. Average lifetime is roughly 1/churn: 1/0.05 = 20 months, 1/0.04 = 25 months, so about a 25% increase, not a doubling. Doubling would require churn of 2.5%.

It's still a real improvement, and at constant margins it raises LTV by about the same 25%. Two checks before you celebrate: a one-point move in a single month can be noise, so confirm it holds over a few months, and blended churn can shift with cohort mix (e.g., fewer new, high-churn customers) without any retention improvement. Compare churn by cohort to be sure.
